seoTitle: Keyboard, Monitor & Desk Phone Sanitizing: Included or Billed Extra?
metaDescription: Audit if keyboard, monitor & desk phone sanitizing is included in base janitorial retainers or billed extra at $1.75-$4.50/desk. Use our Quote Comparator.
excerpt: Nearly 85% of commercial office janitorial contracts include a liability exclusion barring night cleaners from touching computer keyboards, monitors, and plugged-in peripherals. Learn which desktop tasks are included in your base monthly retainer and when an extra-charge IT sanitizing rider is justified.
quickAnswer: In standard US commercial cleaning contracts ($0.07 to $0.15 per sq ft), sanitizing exposed empty desk laminate and common-area conference phones is often included, but individual workstation keyboard, monitor & desk phone sanitizing is almost universally excluded for IT liability reasons. Adding dedicated workstation peripheral sanitizing carries an extra charge of $1.75 to $4.50 per desk per visit (or $35 to $65 per labor hour) under a signed electronics liability addendum.

blocks.text: Why Standard Janitorial Contracts Exclude Workstation Computers and Monitors

One of the most common points of friction between corporate office managers and commercial Building Service Contractors (BSCs) occurs during quarterly quality walkthroughs: the facility manager runs a finger across a dusty monitor bezel or sticky keyboard and asks why the night crew skipped it, while the account manager points to Paragraph 4 of the Statement of Work (SOW) titled 'Electronic Equipment Exclusion.'

Across the US commercial janitorial industry, standard base retainers—priced at $0.12 to $0.20 per sq ft under 2,500 sq ft, $0.09 to $0.15 per sq ft for 2,500 to 9,999 sq ft, and $0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft for 10,000 to 24,999 sq ft—explicitly prohibit general cleaners from touching keyboards, mice, LCD/LED monitors, laptop docks, and cable harnesses. This exclusion exists for two reasons: property damage liability (general quaternary disinfectants ruin anti-reflective screen coatings) and data integrity (wiping an active keyboard on an unlocked terminal can delete data or trigger unauthorized messages).

blocks.text: When Can You Negotiate Desk Phone and Keyboard Wiping Into Your Base Retainer?

Not every extra charge for workstation IT peripherals sanitizing is set in stone. When bidding a new janitorial contract or renewing an annual agreement, you have significant leverage to fold basic peripheral wiping into the base square-foot price under three specific scenarios:

items: Scenario 1: VoIP Desk Phones Only (Excluding Screens & Keyboards): Hard-wired desk phone handsets and dial pads are molded from durable ABS plastic and carry near-zero risk of data loss or screen etching. Most contractors will agree to include weekly (1x/wk across 4.333 weeks/month) desk-phone receiver sanitizing inside the base retainer at no extra charge if the client requests it during RFP bidding.

Scenario 2: High-Frequency 5x-Week Contracts With Slack Floor Time: In offices paying for 5x-week daily service (21.65 visits/month, 0.90x frequency multiplier), Tuesday and Thursday night trash and floor soil loads are often 30% lighter than Monday or Friday. You can negotiate for the night crew to allocate 30 minutes every Wednesday night to wipe clear, locked keyboards and mice across shared hot-desking pods without raising the monthly retainer—provided the facility supplies the 70% isopropyl alcohol wipes.

Scenario 3: Small Suites Paying the $90 to $135 Per-Visit Minimum: If your 1,500 sq ft office has only 10 desks and already pays a $115 minimum trip charge per visit, the cleaner typically has 15 to 25 minutes of unallocated labor capacity built into that minimum fee. Folding a 10-desk keyboard and phone wipe into the existing visit should cost zero extra labor—only $10 to $15/month for electronics-safe wipes.

blocks.title: RFP Contract Language to Prevent Surprise Add-On Bills
blocks.text: When drafting your janitorial RFP, never write 'dust and sanitize all desks.' Instead, specify: 'Weekly Wednesday Service: Sanitize all workstation VoIP telephone handsets/keypads and locked keyboard/mouse surfaces on cleared desks using client-approved 70% IPA wipes; exclude LCD/LED monitor glass unless flagged by IT.' Clear scope language prevents post-award change orders.
When an Extra Charge for IT Peripherals Sanitizing Is Legitimate

Conversely, a contractor is fully justified in quoting a separate monthly line item ($1.75 to $4.50 per workstation) or a standalone project work order ($35 to $65/hr standard labor, or $55 to $95/hr specialty tech detailing) when the scope expands beyond a quick top-surface pass:

items: Dual and Ultra-Wide Monitor Glass Detailing: Polishing smudge-prone LCD panels without streaking or damaging anti-glare coatings requires two separate cloths (one dampened with optical solution, one dry buffing microfiber) and adds 60 to 90 seconds per workstation.

Compressed-Gas Key Channel Extraction: Blowing debris out from beneath mechanical or scissor-switch keys and swabbing between key rows requires canned difluoroethane gas or rechargeable ESD-safe air blowers and cuts production rates from 22 desks/hour down to 10 desks/hour.

Consumable Isolation & Cart Logistics: A professional contractor must isolate electronics sanitizing supplies from general restroom and floor tools. On well-run contracts, crews organize a Rubbermaid Commercial High-Capacity Janitorial Cleaning Cart (with its locking cabinet, 34-gallon zippered vinyl bag, and 40% expanded shelf capacity) so electronics wipes and optical cloths never touch general washroom supplies like Pacific Blue Basic Folded Paper Towels (4,000-count EPA-compliant multifold case) or bulk waste collected in a Rubbermaid Commercial Brute 44-Gallon Vented Trash Can (NSF-listed LLDPE barrel with 50% lower liner-pull resistance).

blocks.text: The Mandatory IT Liability Waiver: What Facility Managers Must Sign

Whether workstation IT peripheral sanitizing is folded into your monthly retainer or billed as an add-on rider, reputable janitorial firms will require a signed 'Electronics & IT Peripheral Cleaning Addendum' before their crew touches a single keyboard. Make sure your addendum establishes fair responsibilities for both sides:

items.name: Define the Chemical Spec & Exclusion List
items.text: Mandate 70% isopropyl alcohol (IPA) or OEM-approved quaternary electronics wipes for plastics, and alcohol-free/ammonia-free optical cleaner for screens. Prohibit trigger spraying directly onto hardware; liquid must always be applied to the cloth or dispensed via pre-wrung wipes.

items.name: Establish the 'Unlocked Screen = Skip Desk' Rule
items.text: Protect both your company's cybersecurity and the janitorial crew by stipulating that if an employee leaves a computer monitor unlocked with active applications open, the technician must skip the keyboard and mouse and log the desk number on the night supervisor report.

items.name: Distinguish Negligent Chemical Damage from Pre-Existing Hardware Wear
items.text: Do not sign a blanket waiver absolving the vendor of all negligence. The contractor's commercial general liability (CGL) policy should remain responsible if an employee sprays bleach or glass cleaner onto an LCD monitor, while absolving the vendor of pre-existing dead pixels, worn keycap lettering, or loose display cables.

faqs.q: If our contract says 'sanitize all high-touch surfaces,' does that legally include computer keyboards?
faqs.a: In standard commercial janitorial terminology (ISSA standards), 'high-touch surfaces' refers to architectural and common-area fixtures: entry door pulls, push plates, elevator buttons, light switches, conference table edges, breakroom appliance handles, and restroom faucets. Personal workstation IT hardware is excluded unless the contract explicitly enumerates 'keyboards, mice, and desk phones.'

faqs.q: How much should an add-on rider for weekly keyboard and phone sanitizing cost in a 50-desk office?
faqs.a: In a 50-desk office (typically 6,000 to 8,500 sq ft) already receiving regular nightly service, a weekly (1x/week, 4.333 visits/month) Tier 1 sanitizing pass for keyboards, mice, and desk phones should cost roughly $2.25 to $3.25 per desk per week—or $487 to $704 per month bundled into your invoice.

faqs.q: Can we ask the night crew to only sanitize desks that have a 'Please Clean' tent card?
faqs.a: Yes, and this is one of the best cost-control methods for hybrid offices. Employees who worked onsite place a laminated green tent card on their locked keyboard before leaving; the night crew only sanitizes flagged desks and bills either a fractional hourly block ($35 to $65/hr) or a tallied per-desk rate based on the nightly log.

faqs.q: Are conference room touchscreens and Zoom Room tablets included or billed extra?
faqs.a: Because conference room AV control tablets (Crestron, iPad, Logitech Tap) are shared common-area touchpoints, most commercial contractors will include wiping them with a dry or lightly dampened optical microfiber cloth during nightly conference room table resetting at no extra charge, provided you supply or specify the screen-safe cloth.
